extracted.intended_audience: applicants seeking registration to practice before the USPTO and their counsel (persons petitioning USPTO Director under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d))
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and litigating a petition to the Director of the USPTO seeking review of an OED Director final decision denying registration to practice before the USPTO (e.g., denial for failure to demonstrate good moral character and reputation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good moral character and reputation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO requires agents, attorneys, or other persons being recognized as representatives of applicants or other persons, to show that they are of good moral character and reputation prior to registration. 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D); 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(a)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant must demonstrate that he presently possesses the good moral character and reputation required to represent applicants before the USPTO; failure to meet this burden supports denial of registration. The OED Director investigates and determines whether the requirement is satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director authority and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director receives and acts on applications for registration, including investigations into moral character and reputation. 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.2(b)(2)-(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual dissatisfied with the final decision of the OED Director may petition the USPTO Director for review under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d). The petition process, including filing location and fee requirements, is governed by the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixty-day filing deadline for petitions under § 11.2(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must be filed with the OED Director within sixty days of the mailing date of the final decision of the OED Director. 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions not filed within sixty days shall be dismissed as untimely. Timeliness of both the petition document and any required fee is material to whether the petition will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must be accompanied by required fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must be accompanied by payment of the appropriate fee required under 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(5)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition filed without timely payment of the required fee may be dismissed. Instructions to charge a deposit account must be effective at the time of filing (i.e., the filer must be an authorized user when the charge is requested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary-situation standard for suspension/waiver of rules (§ 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may seek suspension of any requirement of these rules "[i]n an extraordinary situation." 37 C.F.R. § 11.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver or suspension is only appropriate where a compelling, extraordinary situation is shown. Mere administrative delay or internal firm errors are insufficient; if an extension under § 11.3 has been granted, the petitioner should use that time to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of fee payment and authorization to charge deposit account
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the petition and the fee due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(5)(ii) were required to be filed by the petition deadline (e.g., August 8, 2008).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is considered filed when properly authorized/charged; if the filer is not an authorized user on the deposit account at the time the instruction is given, the charge (and payment) may not be effective until authorization and charging actually occur. Agency records (e.g., Online Shopping Page timestamps) control whether authorization existed at the relevant time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized user status on Deposit Account controls charging ability
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized user must be on the list of authorized users for the Deposit Account in order to instruct a charge; absence from the list prevents the charge from being effected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO's Office of Financial Management Systems records (e.g., timestamp of addition to authorized users via the Online Shopping Page) are used to determine when a person became an authorized user. If payment is made only after an authorized user actually authorizes the charge, the petition's filing/payment date is the later effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's burden of proof to establish moral character and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner bears the burden of establishing to the satisfaction of the OED Director that he presently possesses the good moral character and reputation required to represent applicants before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation and responses to Show Cause requirements must be sufficient to meet this burden; mere assertions without adequate evidentiary support will not satisfy the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of untimely petition or fee (dismissal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition not filed within the regulatory time (or without timely payment of the required fee) is subject to dismissal as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal for untimeliness is generally without prejudice to reapplication; the decision notes that proceedings are concluded but reapplication may be made pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of granted extensions/suspensions to ensure compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a suspension/extension under § 11.3 has been granted to obtain additional time to file, the petitioner must use that time to take all steps necessary to ensure the petition and fee are filed in accordance with § 11.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to complete necessary administrative steps during an extension (e.g., ensuring authorized-user status for payment) does not create an extraordinary situation justifying further waiver; the grant of an extension implies responsibility to act within the extended time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication permitted after dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismissal of a petition for untimeliness is without prejudice to any reapplication for registration to practice before the USPTO that applicant may file in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the current petition is dismissed, the applicant may start a new application process and must comply with the registration rules in effect at that time.
